ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A bush has 10 branches. Each branch has either 5 leaves only or 2 leaves and 1 flower. Can the bush have a total of 37 leaves? Answer yes or no.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let x be the number of branches that have 5 leaves only. Then the remaining 10 - x branches have 2 leaves and 1 flower. The total number of leaves is 5x + 2(10 - x) = 5x + 20 - 2x = 20 + 3x. To have 37 leaves, we would need 20 + 3x = 37, so 3x = 17 and x = 17/3. Since x must be a whole number of branches, this is impossible. Therefore, the bush cannot have exactly 37 leaves.

method.method_draft: Start from the case where all 10 branches are of the 2-leaf-and-1-flower type. Then the bush has 10 × 2 = 20 leaves. Every time one branch is changed from this type to a 5-leaf-only branch, the total number of leaves increases by 5 - 2 = 3. Therefore possible leaf totals are 20, 23, 26, 29, 32, 35, 38, 41, 44, 47, and 50. Since 37 is not in this list, the bush cannot have 37 leaves; answer no.
